French authorities have imposed overnight curfews in Paris and several other cities following a weekend of nationwide protests that descended into widespread rioting and looting. More than 2,500 people have been arrested, with at least two deaths reported and around 1,000 police officers injured. More than 2,000 businesses were affected, with damage estimated at hundreds of millions of euros. ... Italy’s government plans to deploy 500 troops to Milan after weekend protests over rising living costs and public services descended into rioting and looting. Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini announced the move as luxury retailers boarded up windows and removed merchandise. Police arrested 32 people, most of them minors, while a business association estimated damage exceeding €1 million. ... Ukraine’s 92nd Separate Assault Brigade says it has evacuated a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone, in what it describes as a world first. The soldier was lifted by an Ayudag-6 hexacopter and taken to a safer position, where comrades arranged his transfer to hospital. He is now undergoing treatment and rehabilitation. ... Both Ukraine and Russia rely extensively on battlefield drones, creating areas where movement carries substantial danger. Ukraine has previously used unmanned ground vehicles to retrieve casualties but this is its first reported aerial evacuation. Australian independent MP Helen Haines remains in critical but stable condition after a driver allegedly struck her with a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday. Ms. Haines has lost one leg already as a result of the attack and doctors are fighting to save the other one. Witnesses said the vehicle turned towards the 65-year-old lawmaker before hitting her. Haines was airlifted to Melbourne. A 43-year-old man remains in custody. Police believe he acted alone. ... US President Donald Trump said he would consider a three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, but insisted its focus should be nuclear disarmament rather than Ukraine. Putin reportedly proposed talks alongside next month’s APEC summit in China to discuss ending the war. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed discussions about a meeting but said neither its format nor agenda was settled. ... The World Food Programme has cut monthly food assistance in Gaza from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million after its funding fell to less than half previous levels. Families now receive one food parcel instead of two, cash payments have been reduced, and daily hot meals have fallen from 250,000 to 150,000. The agency warns that recent improvements in food security could quickly reverse. ... Japan launched its Martian Moons Exploration spacecraft aboard an H3 rocket on Tuesday, beginning a five-year mission to collect samples from Phobos, the larger of Mars’ two moons. The spacecraft separated successfully after launch from Tanegashima Island. No mission has previously returned material from Mars or either moon, and earlier attempts to reach Phobos have failed. ... US President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 31%, the lowest of either presidential term, as rising fuel prices weigh on voters ahead of November’s congressional elections. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found 47% of registered voters favour Democrats against 35% for Republicans, widening the opposition’s lead from seven to 12 percentage points in two weeks.

items.title: Gold eases as higher oil prices stoke inflation concerns
items.excerpt: Published Tue, Oct 20 2026 12:56 AM EDT Updated 4 Hours Ago ... Gold inched higher on Tuesday, helped by a softer U.S. dollar, as market participants looked ahead to next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting for clues on the future path of interest rates. Chris Ratcliffe | Bloomberg | Getty Images ... Gold edged lower on ​Tuesday as rising oil ​prices stoked inflation ​concerns, with investors looking to next week's Federal Reserve meeting for clues on the US interest-rate outlook. Spot gold fell 0.5% to $4,120.49 per ounce ⁠by ‌0909 GMT. US gold futures for December ⁠delivery dropped 0.5% to $4,139.10 per ounce. "Persistent inflationary pressures, driven by high energy prices, continue to support expectations of further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve," said Ricardo Evangelista, ActivTrades director ‌and CEO. Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a ​geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. "The Fed is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged in October, so the ⁠main focus will be on its guidance regarding a possible increase in ‌December," Evangelista added. Recent comments from Fed officials ‌signalling little urgency for further policy tightening have tempered expectations of a rate hike at the central bank's October 27-28 policy meeting, but traders see a ⁠90% chance of a hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch ⁠Tool. Although gold is traditionally considered an inflation hedge, ⁠higher rates dent its appeal as investors prefer yield-bearing assets. The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the central bank's preferred inflation ​gauge, due next week is ‌also on investors' radar for clues on the interest-rate outlook.

items.title: Hassett Says CPI Data Shows Inflation Needs ‘Some Work’
items.excerpt: (Bloomberg) -- White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said prices have been falling for items such as beef and eggs, though consumer price data for September shows overall inflation continues to need policy attention. "If you look at the previous three months, it looked like inflation was completely under control, and now it looks like it's sort of back needing some work," Hassett told CNBC Monday. Data last week showed consumer prices advanced in September at the fastest pace in five months and a gauge of underlying price pressures rose by more than expected. The consumer price index rose 0.6% from a month earlier while a key measure of underlying price pressures, which excludes food and energy, was up 0.3%. "This is either a sort of break from the downtrend or a blip," Hassett said in the interview. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh last week did nothing to dispel market expectations that the central bank will hold interest rates steady when it meets at the end of the month. In a moderated discussion at the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings, Warsh made no remarks on monetary policy or his outlook for the US economy, apart from reiterating that the Fed will deliver price stability. ... "People are really euphoric about how well the economy is doing, and they're spending more. And of course, that's the kind of thing the Fed needs to pay attention to," Hassett said.

That's down from 56% in May and the fewest since spring 2025. The count borrows a test from Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, who laid it out at Jackson Hole in August. He ... By that yardstick, September looked better than its hotter-than-expected headline. The 12-month count slipped to about 47% from 51% in August. At the 2022 peak, about 4 in 5 categories topped 3%. In the two decades before the pandemic, about 1 in 3 typically did. A narrower spread strengthens the case for waiting, and traders have leaned that way. The bond market put the odds of a hike at the Oct. 27-28 meeting at about 17% by Friday's close, according to Bloomberg data — down from roughly 33% after Wednesday's CPI report. Warsh declined to preview his next move in remarks Friday before the International Monetary Fund. ... ## The holdout categories are the expensive ones ... Electricity, rent, hospital services, and car repairs have all been rising faster than 3% over the past six months, after adjusting for seasonal swings. Gasoline is up about 34% from a year ago. Together, the categories still above the line make up at least 60% of the CPI basket, which the BLS weights by how much households spend on each item. Groceries show the other side of the problem. Grocery prices rose less than 2% over the past year, yet they're still up nearly a third since December 2019. Electricity is up 43% over the same stretch. ... Not everyone sees progress. "There is little evidence of a cooling or a broad-based disinflationary impulse," RSM chief economist Joe Brusuelas wrote Wednesday, pointing to trade, energy, and AI as sources of stubborn price pressure. He expects another quarter-point hike in December. ... The next test arrives Oct. 29, when September PCE inflation is released, one day after the Fed decides. Next month's CPI report follows. If the six-month count holds below 40%, the case for waiting gets stronger. A return to 50% or more — near where it sat for most of the first half of the year — would put a hike back on the table.

items.title: Trump continues midterm campaign blitz in North Carolina
items.excerpt: We start today with Donald Trump’s upcoming to trip to Greenville, North Carolina – where he’ll stump for Michael Whatley, the Republican nominee for US Senate, facing an uphill battle against Roy Cooper, the state’s former Democratic governor who has consistently led Whatley in the polls for the open seat. North Carolina is the president’s second stop in a seven-day campaign blitz across a number of states that he won in 2024. It’s all to drum up support for Republican candidates on the ballot ahead of the midterms – now just two weeks away. However, earlier this month, the Senate’s top GOP Super Pac announced it pulled a $71m ad spend in North Carolina, in order to funnel more money into the Kansas race – a sign that Republicans’ hopes to hold on to the Tar Heel state might be dwindling. ... items.excerpt: Entertainment News (10/21/26) - BusinessWorld Online # Entertainment News (10/21/26) PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. October 20, 2026 | 6:06 pm ## Ziv, VVINK release collaboration PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. Released under Sony Music Entertainment, it is built around Filipino wordplay that links a tricycle’s three wheels to the feeling of being the extra person in someone else’s love story. The song was co-written by Ziv alongside Paolo Benjamin Guico of Filipino folk-pop band Ben&Ben and Angelika Samantha Ortiz, one of the songwriters behind BINI’s hit “Pantropiko.” The mixing was also done by Jacques Jenkins and mastering by Luna Tebbs. The track is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## *Love in Disguise* premieres on Prime Video *LOVE in Disguise*, a Korean series based on the hit web novel *Why Don’t You Know It’s a Girl?*, has premiered on Prime Video. It is directed by Park Dhan-hee and stars Yim Si Wan, Seorina, Kim Junghyun, and Yeonwoo. The genre-blending romance is exclusively seen on Prime Video in the Philippines and in more than 240 countries and territories worldwide. ## Estelle Fly drops club-pop single SINGAPOREAN pop artist Estelle Fly has released “Shut It Down,” a playful club-pop single about switching off the overthinking and making the dance floor your own. Inspired by the Rihanna and Kesha songs, the new release is an invitation to let loose, dance with friends and have fun even when life feels complicated. It is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## Cayabyab, APO, Mitch Valdes reunion THIS holiday season, National Artist for Music Ryan Cayabyab, OPM legends APO, and performer Mitch Valdes will come together for *naRyan nAPO Kami*, the fourth chapter of the MaestroClass Concert Series. The shows will be held on Dec. 4, 5, and 6 at the Proscenium Theater at Rockwell Center, Makati. All shows take place at 7:30 p.m. Joined by the Ryan Cayabyab Singers, the special Christmas chapter of the concert series brings together familiar songs, stories, and artists in a celebration that captures the warmth and spirit of a Filipino family gathering. Tickets are available directly at the Proscenium Theater website via *https://prosceniumtheater.com/* and at the Power Plant Mall Cinema. ## *Amir* gets international distribution GMA Pictures, GMA Public Affairs, and Brightburn Entertainment have officially locked in a partnership deal with Columbia Pictures for the distribution of the upcoming fantasy-drama film and 52 nd Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF) finalist *Amir*. It is directed by Zig Dulay, with a script crafted by National Artist for Film and Broadcast Arts Ricky Lee alongside Anj Atienza. The film’s cast features Dennis Trillo, Argus Aspiras, Glaiza de Castro, Will Ashley, Caprice Cayetano, Epy Quizon, Joel Saracho, Ronnie Lazaro, Laila Ulao, Heath Jornales, Yasser Marta, Mad Ramos, Ethan Hariot, Hebron Ecal, and Mon Confiado. ## Rachel Chinouriri releases new album UK’s indie-pop singer-songwriter Rachel Chinouriri has released her second studio album, I think I spoke too soon, via Atlas Artists/Parlophone Records. The album expands upon the pop, indie, and rock influences that Ms. Chinouriri has long used to sketch portraits of her inner world. The album’s focus track is “Pretty girls,” which celebrates women, self-confidence, and the freedom to express oneself without fear of judgement. ## M2M 2027 world tour has Manila leg NORWEGIAN pop duo M2M have announced that their global tour *TWO* will be coming to Manila in 2027. The tour will start in March and after concerts at Mexico, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Jakarta, M2M’s global tour will reach Manila on April 2, 2027, at the Araneta Coliseum in Quezon City. Tickets will go on sale on Oct. 24 at 10 a.m. via *TicketNet.com.ph* and TicketNet outlets nationwide. Presented by Wilbros Live, the concert will feature M2M performing their greatest hits, “Don’t Say You Love Me,” “Mirror Mirror,” “Pretty Boy,” and “The Day You Went Away,” among others. ## Maris Racal appears in Maya Black’s music video ACTRESS Maris Racal is featured in Maya Black’s latest music video, serving edgy looks against a hyperpop track. In the video, everything she wants turns into a miniature version of itself, bringing the song’s “make it mini” message to life. The idea behind it is all about having more flexibility when it comes to bigger purchases, to promote Maya’s Mini Payments offering. The music video starring Maris Racal can be viewed here: *https://youtu.be/b\_zKjZ6u2f4?si=q8AzbC9iUSLp0sAV*. With Mini Payments, eligible purchases made using the Maya Black credit card can be converted into three, six, nine, or 12 monthly payments.

items.excerpt: Paramount's “Street Fighter” leads the box office this weekend, earning $31 million from 3,575 theaters in the U.S. and Canada. However, the spotlight is on the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything,” which made an impressive $15 million from just 855 screens. Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the film has received rave reviews and a 99% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Meanwhile, the survival thriller “Whalefall” underperformed, earning $8 million domestically. The weekend's overall ticket sales reached about $101.6 million, marking a 45% increase from last year. ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (AP) — A New Mexico judge has dismissed a grand jury indictment that accused actor Timothy Busfield him of four counts of criminal sexual contact with a child. The judge cited prosecutorial misconduct and errors that undermined the grand jury process. The case stems from when Busfield was directing the TV series “The Cleaning Lady.” Busfield denied the allegations, describing them as a vendetta pursued by the parents of two boys who were let go from the show. His attorneys said prosecutors suppressed evidence and restricted grand jury testimony. Prosecutors disputed those claims. NEW YORK (AP) — Selma Blair's representatives have stated she did not intend to harm anyone during a recent flight incident. Blair, who has multiple sclerosis, experienced a medical emergency on a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York. She was accused of injuring two flight attendants and later kicking a police officer and a nurse. Her representatives emphasized that Blair's condition can cause episodes that may be misunderstood. Blair pleaded not guilty to assault charges and is free on bail. The FBI has also charged her with assault related to her actions on the plane. It’s also modestly budgeted at $40 million. And it stars the relatively unknown Tom Rhys Harries as a little-known DC villain.
